messages:
pagerbot: PAGER ALERT: P1 - multiple runtime pods entering CrashLoopBackOff across eu-prod-cluster (svc/runtime). Auto-escalation to oncall-sre.

ashley: seeing ~30% of runtime pods restart in the last 6m, start count pileups. node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-21 show repeated kubelet restarts.

matt: logs from one of the pods:
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] runtime-engine: fatal error: signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
#0  0x7f8b2a1d4f20 in vllm::TensorRTBackend::launch() at trt_backend.cpp:312
#1  0x7f8b2a1c9aa2 in vllm::Runtime::serve_batch() at runtime.cpp:498
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): CUDA error: out of memory (attempted to allocate 8.00 GiB)
```

lina: stack points to TensorRT custom kernel (libtrt_custom.so) and a vLLM wrapper. Not just OOM — signal 11 after attempted allocation. Could be invalid device pointer from kernel.

ashley: GPU summary from node-gpu-17: `nvidia-smi` shows GPU0 memory jitter then process killed by SIGSEGV. Also `dmesg` shows `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31` followed by `show_stack`.

devon: customer-impact: 6 customers (including higher tier tenants) reporting 5xx generation failures and streaming disconnects since 18:00. Error rate spiked to 12% for API /v1/generate. Notified customer success.

matt: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce model footprint (route to smaller model variant), 2) cordon problematic nodes and shift pods, 3) roll back latest runtime kernel module if we deployed one last night.

ashley: taking node-swap approach now: cordon node-gpu-17, drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`, evict pods, and let autoscaler reschedule onto healthy nodes. Doing one node at a time.

ashley: command: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-17 && kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

opsbot: DEPLOY BOT: Notified engine team of pod restarts linked to commit b3f2a7a (trt-alloc-improv). No automated rollback configured.

lina: quick binary check — we saw an unusual symbol mismatch between libtrt_custom.so (from build b3f2a7a) and system libnvinfer. If the TRTRuntime ABI changed, device pointers can be invalidated. Suggest pinning nodes to older image for a hotfix rollout.

matt: I'm going to scale down batchers to avoid large allocations: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime --containers=runtime BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512` and `BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=50` to reduce peak memory. Applying now.

ashley: scaled batch env vars, reducing concurrency. Watching pod restarts.

ashley: drain completed on node-gpu-17, pods rescheduled to node-gpu-04 and node-gpu-09. node-gpu-21 still showing occasional kernel oops.

devon: customer impact update — for the affected customers errors are 5xx with body {"error":"runtime failure: internal"}. We've opened an incident page and notified 2 enterprise customers directly with ETA for mitigation.

lina: proposed action plan: 1) patch libtrt_custom.so to add bounds checks (short-term), 2) revert to runtime image tag `runtime:2026-03-10` for production (rollback), 3) bake a device-swap fallback in the scheduler (long-term). Who can coordinate rollback?

matt: I can push rollback to canary then prod. Plan: 1) deploy `runtime:2026-03-10-canary` to 10% traffic and monitor for 10m, 2) if stable, bump to 100% over 15m. Rolling now to canary.

ashley: heads-up: during rollback we may still see residual node flapping if kernel driver crashed. I'm coordinating with infra to restart the NVIDIA driver on node-gpu-21 if it repeats.

opsbot: INFRA ACTION: scheduled `systemctl restart nvidia-docker` on node-gpu-21 in 60s, will report back.

matt: canary rollout applied. New pods show no immediate segfaults after 2m, memory profiles look stable.

ashley: node-gpu-21 had one more `Xid 79` and kubelet restarted; infra restarted driver, node ready. Monitoring cluster-wide for 20m.

devon: customers report reduced errors to ~2% from 12%. Sending update to customer success to resume notifications.

lina: next steps: create a postmortem checklist item to add ABI compatibility tests between custom TRT libs and system libnvinfer across driver versions. Also add a pre-deploy smoke that runs a tiny TensorRT workload on each node type.

matt: handoff to next oncall: @ashley I'll let you take ownership for the remainder of the night for monitoring and follow-up. Ping me if we see any regressions.

ashley: taking handoff. I'll keep the channel open and post a short incident summary and timelines to the incident tracker.

pagerbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> P1 -> P2 (reduced customer impact). Please fill in postmortem template and tag `#incidents`.

ashley: summary to paste into tracker: "Crashwave caused by incompatible TRT custom kernel (commit b3f2a7a) leading to device-side allocation/assert -> SIGSEGV and container crashloops. Hot mitigations: cordon/drain affected nodes, scale down batching, rollback runtime image to 2026-03-10, restart nvidia driver on flapping nodes, route traffic away from canary during verification. Impact: 12% error spike, 6 customers affected, reduced to ~2% after mitigation."

devon: added customer impact notes and notified CS. Closing handoff.

matt: filing PR to revert the risky changes and add unit test for pointer lifetime.

lina: creating follow-up ticket for runtime-eng: ABI compatibility smoke + device-swap fallback in scheduler.

ashley: thanks all. I am leaving the channel open and will update if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
